pointers.sentence: A comment calls the construct somewhat of an abuse of `ForeignObject`: the relation runs from the key to the object id, but its join is made the other way, as along a foreign key from the note, so the object id is the from-field (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericRelation.__init__`).

`ForeignObject.__init__` uses its `on_delete` only to make a rel when it is given none, and `GenericRelation` gives it a `GenericRel`, made with `DO_NOTHING`, as the run found (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericRel`).

`GenericRelation.contribute_to_class` joins the class with `private_only=True`, so the field is kept in `Options.private_fields`, as a `GenericForeignKey` is, and not among the local fields; and it puts a `ReverseGenericManyToOneDescriptor` under its name (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericRelation.contribute_to_class`).

If the note model is ordered with respect to the matching generic key, the lighthouse model gets the two order methods a foreign key would give it (`django/db/models/base.py:make_foreign_order_accessors`).

`GenericRelation.get_path_info` gives the one hop a query takes from the lighthouse to the note, made as the reverse of a foreign key is, with the rel as its join field; `GenericRelation.get_reverse_path_info` gives the hop back, with the field itself (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericRelation.get_path_info`).

The content type comes from `GenericRelation.get_extra_restriction`: an exact lookup of the note's content type column against the key of the lighthouse model's content type, which `Join.as_sql` adds to the ON clause in parentheses (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`).

A rel hands the question to its field with the two aliases swapped, so the condition falls on the note's table whichever way the join runs (`django/db/models/fields/reverse_related.py:ForeignObjectRel.get_extra_restriction`).

`GenericRel` takes it for its related name too, so the note model also gets an attribute of that name, a manager of the lighthouses, set as for the other end of any `ForeignObject` (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignObject.contribute_to_related_class`).

`ReverseGenericManyToOneDescriptor` is the reverse descriptor of a foreign key with another manager class: `create_generic_related_manager` subclasses the note model's default manager's class (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:ReverseGenericManyToOneDescriptor.related_manager_cls`).

Its queryset is what `prefetch_related` left on the lighthouse, if anything, and otherwise the default manager's, filtered so, in the lighthouse's fetch mode ([Deferred fields and the fetch modes](../instance/fetching.md)) (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:create_generic_related_manager`).

`Collector.collect` asks each private field of the model that has a `bulk_related_objects` for more rows, and collects them in turn (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.collect`); the same attribute stops `Collector.can_fast_delete` letting the lighthouses be deleted unseen ([Deleting: the `Collector`](../instance/deleting.md)).

`GenericRelation.bulk_related_objects` answers with the note model's base manager on the collector's database, filtered by the content type's key and the keys being deleted (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericRelation.bulk_related_objects`).

`generic_inlineformset_factory` takes the note model and the names of its two fields; it refuses a content type field that is not a foreign key to `ContentType` with a bare `Exception`, excludes both fields from the forms, makes the class with `modelformset_factory`, and sets the two fields and `for_concrete_model` on it (`django/contrib/contenttypes/forms.py:generic_inlineformset_factory`).

Made with an instance, the formset's queryset is the notes of the default manager, or of the queryset it is given, for the instance's content type and key, or none for an instance without a key, and `BaseGenericInlineFormSet.save_new` sets the two fields on each new note (`django/contrib/contenttypes/forms.py:BaseGenericInlineFormSet`).

`GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset` reads the same hooks as `InlineModelAdmin.get_formset` and calls `generic_inlineformset_factory` with `ct_field` and `ct_fk_field` where the other names a foreign key; its form ignores changes the user may not make, but lacks the other's refusal to delete a row that protected objects point at (`django/contrib/contenttypes/admin.py:GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset`) ([Inlines: `InlineModelAdmin` and its formsets](../admin/inlines.md)).

`GenericInlineModelAdminChecks` replaces the check of the foreign key with one that the model has a `GenericForeignKey` on the two named fields, `"admin.E301"` to `"admin.E304"` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/admin.py:GenericInlineModelAdminChecks._check_relation`).
